units: metres, Y up, origin at the centre of the 100 mm cube (CAD: millimetres, Z up; the antenna deploys along CAD +Z = glTF +Y)

sources.original: 3d models/cubesat/madhav/ffpcb.stp (Creo export of fpcb_asm_1.asm): flex-PCB base, Arduino Nano, MPU6050, MOSFET, transmitter module, battery holder, 18650 cell, spring. Placement is mine; the STEP leaves them unmated.
sources.reconstructed: frame, standoffs, antenna cassette, burn-wire hardware, tape antenna: modelled here; no original geometry exists in a readable form.

antenna.kind: steel tape-spring antenna (the case study says 'steel tape antenna'); stored energy is the coiled tape's elastic strain
antenna.axis_note: reel axis is the cassette's Y; the straight tape leaves at x=exit_x, directed +Z; all x/z values are relative to the cassette origin

sequence_s_illustrative.note: timing is a depiction, not a measured or specified value

assumptions: Frame: 100 mm cube with 2.5 mm walls. The original Creo frame is unreadable; the 94.8 x 94.0 mm flex-PCB board in the source fits a 95 mm cavity. Window pattern: hexagonal opening, ribs and four screw holes per face are modelled on the Fusion study screenshots, not measured.
Top and bottom plates: ring of wedge slots modelled on the study screenshot of the top plate; the bottom plate is assumed to match.
Component layout: the STEP leaves every component at its own origin (duplicates coincide), so positions inside the frame are my arrangement.
Antenna: tape 8 x 0.4 mm, 190 mm long, transverse curvature 1.4 mm, 150 mm deployed. None of these is from the source; the source has no antenna geometry.
Release: a nylon-style restraint cord across the tape's exit, severed by heated nichrome wire. The case study names a burn-wire mechanism; its geometry is not in the source.
The source's spring (9.3 x 7.3 mm, thin wire) is shown as an original part. Its role in the real design is not documented and it is not animated.
Timing and speed of release and deployment are illustrative.
